text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Foreign ministry director-general Eytan Bentsur says Israel wants no terms to Syrian talks.
- U.S. envoy Dennis Ross to present new peace proposals.
- Holocaust Martyrs' and Heroes' Remembrance Day begins tonight.
- Israeli leader Netanyahu drafts series of gestures to Palestinians ahead of Ross visit -- building for Arabs in Jerusalem and change in law on permanent residents in city.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon warns government will have to resign if it doesn't make some urgent changes such as cancellation of the direct-election law for prime minister.
- Expulsion of illegal foreign workers has nearly completely stopped; 60 deported in April.
- Army chief: Budget doesn't enable us to do all that's needed to prepare for war. Israeli President Ezer Weizman could meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat this week.
- Military intelligence research chief says Syria is certainly preparing a military option.
- Netanyahu meets Finance Minister Dan Meridor on further budget cut.
- Military intelligence research chief: Syrians prepare for war but are still interested in negotiations.
